column12: CMS spending is gross of manufacturer rebates and spending per beneficiary is not a year of therapy: Eliquis beneficiaries fill 487.3 of the 730 tablets a year at 5mg twice daily, 66.8%. Both errors are in the price and they cancel. CMS's negotiated Maximum Fair Price for Eliquis is $231 per 30 days from 1 January 2026, $2,810 a patient-year, and this price net of the convention is $2,353, 16% below it. Eliquis loses exclusivity on 1 April 2028 per Pfizer's 10-K, so an asset launching after that is priced off a branded incumbent that will be generic, and warfarin realises $51 a Part D beneficiary. No premium is carried for the monthly antibody route, because none is measurable: the two marketed cardiovascular-prevention injectables realise no more per Medicare beneficiary than the pills, Repatha Sureclick at $4,470 and Praluent Pen at $3,683, both CMS Part D 2024

column11: twice the 0.03 carried for milvexian and REGN7508, a labelled judgement. The case for the multiple: the pool is patients on no anticoagulant, so there is no incumbent to displace and no stable therapy to switch off, and AZALEA-TIMI 71 cut major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding 67% against rivaroxaban, 10.6% to 3.5% in 1,287 patients, stopped early on the monitoring committee's recommendation
column12: the case against: Novartis' own ASTER trial in cancer-associated thrombosis was halted after the independent data review committee found inferior efficacy to apixaban, which is the mechanism's only completed head-to-head. 0.06 x 0.15 is 0.009 of the atrial fibrillation pool against milvexian's 0.03 x 0.53 = 0.0159, so 57% of its patient flow
